title: Minimax Testing with Negative-Control Outcomes under Weak Proxies
banked_reason: kernel_substituted@oeq:sharp-frontier: the paper's named sharp growing-K frontier remains explicitly open; the delivered package is incremental and below the field floor.
gap_reasons: They do not prove the advertised growing-K separation frontier: the available projection upper bound is generally of order sqrt(K/n) plus training terms, leaving a polynomial gap from the dense lower bound.

Operator-nuisance matching, active-face calibration, adaptation to unknown a, phase transitions, and the maximal K-growth range are all left as open-ended questions, so the central frontier contribution is not delivered.
Stage 0.5 (typed) finding outside D0.R core-edit scope — kernel_substituted@oeq:sharp-frontier.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved a conservative finite-sample projection test, explicit fixed-K root-n upper and lower results, and a legal restricted dense-block lower bound. The advertised sharp growing-K frontier collapsed because the matching centered cross-fit upper theorem, operator-training control, active-face calibration, unknown-a adaptation, phase transitions, and maximal K-growth range remained open. D0.5 therefore found kernel substitution and rated the delivered package incremental.
tldr: The proposal directly tests the observed-law null \(d(P)=0\), where \(\mathcal H_\beta(R,\eta)\) is a user-chosen smooth bounded diagnostic class. The ordered support and label-DCT coordinates are known, while the design metric and conditional-expectation operator are estimated. A split convex program and finite-sample projection inequality supply honest size and a lower confidence bound. The fixed-support root-\(n\) upper bound is now matched unconditionally at \(K=2\) under the base link constants, and for every fixed \(K\) under the explicit DCT compatibility condition, because those constructions furnish one common positive cell, marginal, and link slack over \(a\). Under the same DCT compatibility condition, a legal positive-multinomial dense block gives the \(K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\) obstruction when \(K=o(n^{2/3})\) and \(K^{-(a_L+\beta)}\le c_0K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\). The complete growing-\(K\) phase diagram and valid adaptation to unknown \(a\) remain open questions.
gap: Existing single-NCO diagnostics, inverse-testing results, and convex-projection methods do not give finite-sample uniform testing or a sharp minimax radius for the observed-law null \(d(P)=0\) when a user-chosen bounded source image and its operator are estimated from one growing multinomial table.
fill: The project supplies a deterministic-coordinate split projection upper bound and a fully legal two-label benchmark, then isolates the still-open transverse-path, dense-mixture, active-face, and adaptive-calibration constructions required for a sharp total-error frontier.
